case_number: Constitution Petition bearing W.P. No.15504 of 2015

parties.respondent: Member (Colonies) Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore etc S.No. of Order/ Proceeding

statutes_cited: Section 3(2) of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972
holding: For what has been discussed above, this appeal being devoid of merits is dismissed.

paragraphs.text: MUZAMIL AKHTAR SHABIR, J. The appellant, Masood Ahmad, being aggrieved of dismissal of his Constitution Petition bearing W.P. No.15504 of 2015, vide order dated 25.04.2017 (‘impugned order’), passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court, has filed the instant Intra Court Appeal under Section 3(2) of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972.

Learned counsel for the appellant states that the appellant is aggrieved of the impugned order, whereby the purpose of use of land, subject matter of this appeal, had been converted from Temporary Cultivation Scheme to the Lambardari Grant Scheme, as the same had been passed in conflict with a previous order dated 04.03.2015 passed by this Court in a Constitution Petition bearing W.P. No. 5849 of 2015, earlier filed by the appellant, whereby a right had been created in favour of the appellant for allotment of land under the Temporary Cultivation Lease Scheme read with Government Policy dated 26.11.2013 by competing with the highest bidder in the auction proceedings and the aforementioned conversion has caused prejudice to the right of the appellant.

On the other hand, the learned Law Officer has defended the impugned order by claiming that the government, being the owner of the property subject matter of this petition, is authorized to convert the purpose for use of land retained for one purpose to another.

Brief background of the case is that earlier the appellant filed W.P. No. 5849 of 2015 for seeking setting aside of orders dated 28.08.2014 passed by the Member (Colonies) Board of Revenue, Punjab/ Respondent No.1, whereby appellant’s application for grant of proprietary rights regarding land measuring 76-Kanals 13-Marlas situated in Chak No.76/EB, Tehsil Arif Wala District Pakpattan, subject matter of this petition was dismissed and the Members (Colonies) Board of Revenue directed the District Collector, Pakpattan to resume the disputed land measuring 71-Kanals 18-Marlas, which was illegally occupied by the appellant and also recover Tawan from him. This Court vide order dated 04.03.2015, dismissed the said writ petition being not maintainable and frivolous, however, in paragraph No.8 of the said order following observations were recorded: ‘8. The petitioner being illegal and unauthorized occupant is not entitled to retain the state property measuring 71-Kanals 18-Marlas, as such, the order passed by the Member (Colonies), Board of Revenue Punjab is that land is reserved under Temporary Cultivation Lease Scheme and it will be disposed of in accordance with the Government Policy dated 26.11.2013 is a just and well-reasoned order’.

Side by side, respondent No.3, Mian Allah Ditta filed an application dated 24.01.2013 for conversion of said land to Lambardari Scheme for allotment to him, whereupon this Court vide order dated 28.01.2015 passed in Writ Petition No.2265 of 2015, directed the Member (Colonies) Board of Revenue to decide the application filed by respondent No.3. During the pendency of proceedings before the Member (Colonies), the appellant made an oral request for being impleaded as a party, which was regretted and the land was included in the Lumbardari Scheme vide order dated 18.05.2015. The said order was called in question by the appellant through W.P. No. 15504 of 2015, which has resulted in dismissal of the same through the impugned order.

The sole grievance of the appellant is that the observations recorded by this Court in order dated 04.03.2015 should have been implemented in letter and spirit and the conversion of the purpose of use of land in the circumstances of the case from Temporary Cultivation Scheme to the Lambardari Grant was not justified. It is pertinent to mention here that the land was owned by the Provincial Government and not by the appellant who was an illegal occupant of the said land. The government being owner was fully authorized to define the purpose for which the land was to be used and it could convert its use from one purpose to another on its own free will, which could not be made subject to the whims of an illegal occupant for the reason that such a person has no right to occupy the land without there being a right created in his favour under some provision of law. Reliance may be placed on Muhammad Aslam versus Muhammad Ismail and others (1999 SCMR 1331), wherein it was held as under: "2. The relevant facts are that an application was filed before A.C. Chiniot alleging that the land measuring 36 Kanals forming subject of Chowkidari grant was in illegal possession of the petitioner. An inquiry was held and the allegations were found to be correct. The A.C. Chiniot directed that the crop sown in the land in question be given on Superdari to somebody and if no one was prepared to take the same the Girdawar, should take over it. The petitioner challenged the said order before the Additional Commissioner (Revenue), which was dismissed with the direction that if the petitioner failed to give share to the Mueens the same may be distributed in accordance with law and that the possession of land be also restored to the Mueens by resorting to section 32/34 of Colonization of the Government Lands Act, 1912. Thereafter, the petitioner filed a revision in the Board of Revenue Punjab, which was dismissed. Dissatisfied with the aforesaid orders, he filed a writ petition in the High Court, which too was dismissed. Hence, this petition. 3. The High Court observed that since in the Khasra Girdawari the petitioner had been shown as an illegal occupant of the land in dispute, he was, therefore, not entitled to any relief in the equitable and discretionary jurisdiction of the Court. 4. It is contended that there has been a gross misreading of the revenue papers and that proper opportunity of hearing was not afforded to the petitioner to establish his claim. 5. It is clearly mentioned in the Khasra Girdawari relied upon by the petitioner that he was an illegal occupant of the land in question. As he had failed to show his legal claim on that piece of land, he was rightly not considered entitled to the discretionary relief. Finding no infirmity in the impugned order we dismiss the petition."

Besides, the petitioner cannot base his claim for seeking relief on the observations recorded by the Court in paragraph No. 8 of its order dated 04.03.2015 mentioned above for the reason that those observations were purely tentative in nature and did neither effect the merits of the case nor caused prejudice to any party or create a vested right in favour of the said party for enforcement of the same through the process of law and the revenue authorities while exercising jurisdiction on behalf of the Provincial Government vested in them under the law were well within their jurisdiction to decide the purpose for which the land owned by the government would be used. Hence, the appellant cannot seek enforcement of the same. Reliance is placed upon Dr. Maqbool Ahmed versus Province of the Punjab through Collector, District Rahimyar Khan-and others (2001 SCMR 737), Sardar versus Islamia College Old Boys Cooperative Housing Society Limited (2002 SCMR 1298), SHERI-CBE and others versus Lahore Development Authority and others (2006 SCMR 1202), Haji Amin versus Navaid Hussain and others (2008 SCMR 133), Ahmad Ali alias Ali Ahmad versus Nasar-ud-Din and another (PLD 2009 SC 453), Anjum Aqeel Khan and others versus National Police Foundation through M.D. and others (2015 SCMR 1348), Mian Muhammad Nawaz Sharif and others versus Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi and others (PLD 2018 SC 1) and Abdullah and others versus Waryam and others (2026 SCMR 1042), wherein it is mentioned that observations of the Court based on tentative assessment do not affect the merits of the main case.

Moreover, the appellant has not denied that his possession over the disputed land was unauthorized and he had been declared and treated as an illegal occupant throughout the proceedings, which observations recorded against him had neither been challenged nor dislodged through any material available on record. Relief through extraordinary constitutional jurisdiction was to be granted to an aggrieved person and not to a person who was not aggrieved of impugned order or proceedings. In the instant case, the appellant being an unauthorized occupant was not an aggrieved person in case the said property was allotted by the competent authority to a person held entitled to the same. Reference may be made to Gulistan Textile Mills Ltd., Bahawalpur through Intizar Ahmed, Manager versus Member (Consolidation), Board of Revenue/Chief Settlement Commissioner, Punjab, Lahore and 13 others (1997 MLD 449 Lahore) and Abdul Sattar and others v. Assistant Commissioner, Gujranwala and others (1988 MLD 1321 Lahore). Hence, it is observed that no illegality, jurisdictional defect or mis-reading and non- reading of record has been pointed out in the impugned order.

On the basis of aforementioned reasons, there is no ground for us to warrant interference in the impugned order passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court, whereby the constitution petition, filed by the appellant, has been dismissed.
For what has been discussed above, this appeal being devoid of merits is dismissed. (CH. MUHAMMAD IQBAL) (MUZAMIL AKHTAR SHABIR) JUDGE JUDGE Naveed* APPROVED FOR REPORTING:
